sourceFacts: Bar height, leg position and foot elevation change demand.
Repeatable grip and no sagging hips are emphasized; volume increases sets at fixed demand.
appDecisions: Secured-bar confirmation and recorded height; 1–250 cm is an input-validation range, not a recommended height.
Bent-knee automatic practice only; two-to-four sets of five with 90-second rest.
Changed height starts a separate comparison cycle; changed actual geometry earns no progression credit against the written setup.
limits: The app cannot measure body angle, grip spacing, apparatus strength or actual foot placement.
An opt-in app adaptation of 60%/80% cycling is now implemented; the exact weekly frequency, forced maximum retest, straight-leg automatic prescription and pull-ups remain outside its scope.

entry.purpose: Practice horizontal pulling with bent knees and a stable bar as preparation for more demanding pulling.
setup: Use a secured, load-appropriate stable bar that cannot roll or move off its support. Record its actual height in Settings; no universal height is prescribed.
Lie beneath the bar, use consistent wide hand marks and place feet flat with knees bent. Adjust foot placement for a familiar controlled position.
steps: Engage glutes and abdomen to keep the hips from sagging.
Pull toward the middle of the chest with controlled movement.
Lower with control, retaining the chosen bar height, leg position and repeatable foot placement.
bracing: Keep knee, hip and shoulder alignment controlled, glutes engaged and ribcage controlled. The source does not establish one mandatory breath cadence.
mistakes: Sagging hips: reduce demand and regain the supported line.
Comparing different heights or bent/straight-leg work as the same intensity: record setup changes and do not infer progression from rep count alone.
Using an unsecured or rolling bar: do not begin.

evidence.quote: the lower the bar the harder it is
rep count is entirely up to the athlete
the 80% should be 2/3 of the volume of the 60% day
after four to 6 weeks you could retest your Max

qualifications: The source describes bent-to-straight legs and elevated feet as ways to change demand. Automatic prescriptions currently use bent knees only.

The optional row 60%/80% profile uses the source rep fractions and two-thirds volume relationship. Whole-rep/whole-set rounding, a conservative user-reviewed baseline, paired clean-exposure gates, set endpoints, 90-second rests and rolling scheduling are app choices. The source two-days-each weekly example and optional 4–6-week maximum retest are not imposed. No maximum test is requested.
The selected five-rep, two-to-four-set, 90-second-rest practice is an app adaptation, as are setup matching and qualification thresholds.
Bar height and leg position are tracked, but the user must also keep grip, foot placement and range repeatable. The app cannot measure actual body angle or certify apparatus safety.
